description: Deterministic owner of discovery source identity and behaviour. Source families exist so coverage diversity is measured by real inventory families rather than by nominal site count. This file describes sources only. It never holds candidate preferences, credentials, cookies, account names or private candidate data. Each source also declares which SEARCH families pay off against it and how many result cards are worth inspecting per productive query, so the planner reads those facts rather than a human keeping a prose table in step. Each family also declares a monitoring class, so an omission from a daily plan is a recorded decision rather than an accident.

vocabularies.query_execution_meaning: Whether a requested query is reproducibly EXECUTED, DISPLAYED and VERIFIABLE on this source. `verified` means the rendered page demonstrably reflects the requested query. `unverified` means it could not be confirmed. `ignores_query` means the source was observed returning its unfiltered inventory regardless of the query. Only `verified` may own a mandatory query-specific obligation, because a bucket names a QUERY on an inventory and a source that cannot run the query cannot discharge it.

adzuna.monitoring_reason: WORKING HYPOTHESIS, not a measurement. Adzuna is an aggregator, so its listings are expected to overlap substantially with Reed, CWJobs, Totaljobs and the employer sites this workspace already searches daily, and an aggregated listing is expected to carry a weaker vacancy identity than the employer or board copy it was drawn from. Neither expectation has been measured here: no production run has yet searched Adzuna, so there is no duplicate rate, no unique-candidate count and no filter-compliance observation in this workspace to appeal to. It is classed `rotating` on that expectation alone, which is why the class carries an empirical review rather than a conclusion. It stays enabled and queryable, and exhaustive mode always reaches it.

policy_review_criteria: duplicate rate against records already discovered from other sources
detailed-read efficiency: Direct matches per job description read
freshness-filter compliance observed on its result cards
source failures, access cost and any anti-bot friction
adzuna.policy_review_note: Whichever comes first: three successful runs that actually searched it, or the date backstop. If the measured duplicate rate is low or its unique contribution is material, promote it to `daily`. If the hypothesis holds, keep it rotating and record the numbers that justified it. Do not restate the hypothesis as a finding until the numbers exist.

sources.notes: Downgraded 2026-08-31 from reliable-filter after production run scrape-20260831T083115570281. TWO separate findings. First, sortBy=DD DESTROYS keyword semantics: 'Python Developer' and 'Integration Developer' returned 17 of 18 identical job ids, and 'Python Django REST Framework' returned Splunk Consultant and Document Review Specialist. Never pass sortBy=DD. Second, WITHOUT that parameter the keyword search works correctly and returns genuinely query-specific results, but the card set is Promoted-dominated: across three verification searches only 3 of 16 cards carried any readable posted age while 12 were badged Promoted, so the Date posted filter cannot be verified per card. Read every card's own posted age, and where it is absent treat freshness as unknown and open the vacancy for its own date before counting it.
fromage and sort=date are honoured. Stop on Cloudflare or CAPTCHA rather than bypassing it.

Observed 2026-08-28: the postedwithin filter does not constrain promoted slots. Cards badged PREMIUM or FEATURED appeared under an active Last 24 hours filter showing 1 week ago and 1 month ago. Read every card posted age individually before counting it toward a freshness window.

family_coverage_policy.description: Which inventory families an ordinary run must reach, which rotate, and which are deliberately out of scope. An omission has to be a decision with a reason and a review date. A family quietly missing from every plan looks identical to a family nobody thought about.

classes.rotating: Searched on a documented rolling cycle, not every day.
classes.exhaustive: Reached only by an explicitly requested wide sweep.
classes.excluded: Deliberately not queried. Excluded from every denominator.

family_coverage_policy.notes: Exhaustive mode must reach every enabled, queryable family whose class is not `excluded`; the validator asserts 100 per cent against that denominator. A daily run reaches the daily families plus the rotating families due this cycle, and its plan lists what it omitted and why. Coverage is counted by FAMILY: six sponsor boards inside one family are one family covered, never six, because counting them separately would inflate the number without searching more inventory. A failed or partial run does not advance the cycle, because the families it was supposed to reach were not reached. A rotating family whose own last successful coverage is older than force_due_after_hours becomes due IMMEDIATELY, whatever the cycle position says. Without that override the cycle counts RUNS while the cap counts HOURS, so a workspace run weekly would let a three-run family wait twenty-one days against a fourteen-day cap and lose a week of inventory that nothing could recover. The override is set well below the cap so the pull-forward happens before anything is lost rather than after.
